citation.title: MACHINE LEARNING METHOD IN ELASTIC PLATE TOPOLOGY OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS
citation.authors: D.V. Avdonyushkin, A.I. Matveeva, A.D. Novokshenov

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For a 2D elastic plate, neural networks produce topology predictions in 0.16–0.24 s versus 120 s for MMA optimization; the three-layer network is 750 times faster by the reported times.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: 120 s MMA time divided by 0.16 s three-layer neural-network time (Table 2); the single-layer network gives 120/0.24 = 500 times.
claim.alternatives: Section 5, Table 1 compares elementwise topology errors between the two neural networks; Figures 7–9 show comparisons with MMA designs.

baseline.classical_method: MMA topology optimization with SIMP density parameterization
baseline.implementation: ANSYS finite-element analysis with DS Simulia Tosca Structure
baseline.solver: MMA; FE solver identified as ANSYS, linear solver not stated
baseline.problem_size: 2D square elastic plate; 10,000 finite elements referenced in Section 5
baseline.data_generation_cost: Approximately 3 h 43 min to create the training set (Section 5)
baseline.quality_metric: Elementwise binary topology error against MMA designs; Section 5, Table 1
baseline.quality_gap: Mean errors 29.85 (single-layer) and 10.4 (three-layer); error fractions 0.00597 and 0.00208 (Table 1)

R1.evidence: Section 5, Tables 1–2: output topologies are compared with MMA and elementwise errors are reported, but matching the timed runs by objective quality is not shown and the MMA stopping rule is unstated.

R2.evidence: Section 5, Table 2 gives direct MMA timings, but Sections 3–5 do not identify the hardware or justify the platform comparison.

R3.evidence: Section 5 reports training time and about 3 h 43 min for data generation, but does not amortize these costs or report a break-even use count.

R4.evidence: Section 5, Table 1 evaluates elementwise topology error and Figures 7–9 show examples; returned designs are not reported as FE-verified for compliance and feasibility.

reporting.n_test_cases: 30 force locations used to generate topologies; no separate held-out test count stated (Section 3)

notes: Full-text publisher PDF: https://ered.pstu.ru/index.php/mechanics/article/download/3791/3046. The paper says boundary post-processing is needed but gives no post-processing time in Table 2.
